headline: High risk: Dify’s broad filesystem/network/tooling can amplify Botpress outputs into unsafe actions and data exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress can generate chatbot content, and Dify can wire tools into agent/workflow apps with shared conversation state. Even without an explicit shared clipboard or MCP, Dify’s file and tool surfaces make it plausible that Botpress output is treated as trusted input. The interaction is inferred from docs, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Botpress output is fed into a Dify workflow or agent prompt without sanitization
IF Dify tools consume Botpress-generated text as instructions
mitigations: Add an explicit instruction/content separator in the workflow prompt
Strip or escape tool-like markup from Botpress outputs
Require a human review step before any Dify tool call
Log and flag any Botpress text that contains imperative verbs or JSON
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between Botpress and Dify

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress is open-source with no network egress, but Dify reads uploaded knowledge base files, stores conversation logs, and sends data to model providers and user-defined OpenAPI tools. If Botpress content is routed into Dify, sensitive workspace data can leave the local boundary through Dify’s default integrations. The pairwise leakage path is documented only indirectly, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Botpress-generated content includes secrets or customer data
IF Dify is configured with external model providers or OpenAPI tools
IF uploaded knowledge base files contain regulated data
mitigations: Disable external tools for sensitive conversations
Redact secrets before passing Botpress output into Dify
Restrict Dify knowledge-base uploads to non-sensitive documents
Review provider and tool destinations in Dify settings
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while Dify can execute server-side Python code and write/read files with broad egress. Both can mutate shared artifacts if connected through the same workspace or datastore, creating overlapping write authority even though Botpress’s filesystem surface is not explicit. Because the shared-write path is inferred, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem or shared datastore
IF Botpress package installation changes artifacts consumed by Dify
IF Dify workflows write back to files that Botpress reads
mitigations: Separate Botpress and Dify into different directories
Disable write access for one side in shared environments
Use per-agent service accounts with distinct permissions
Add file locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: introduce transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can produce support answers, and Dify can orchestrate agents and workflows that call tools or model providers. If Dify treats Botpress output as authoritative, a mistaken Botpress answer can cascade into downstream actions or rendered responses. The pairwise dependency is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits the documented analogue.
conditions: IF Dify uses Botpress output as an input to another agent or tool
IF Dify does not verify Botpress facts before acting
IF downstream workflows send emails, update KBs, or trigger APIs
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action
Require citations or source links from Botpress outputs
Limit Dify actions to read-only mode for Botpress-fed flows
Show Botpress output as advisory only
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source and self-hostable, while Dify explicitly stores conversation logs, handles model-provider API keys, and may send data to external providers or tools. If regulated content flows from Botpress into Dify, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in both systems
IF Dify conversation logs retain data longer than Botpress operators expect
IF external model providers or tools receive the same records
mitigations: Set a short retention window for Dify logs
Avoid sending regulated data into Dify workflows
Document residency and vendor destinations for each tool
Purge conversation logs after support sessions
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
